strategies.overview: Bisharp stands out as one of the premier setup sweepers in the metagame due its access to Swords Dance, strong priority in Sucker Punch, and impressive Eviolite-boosted bulk. Coupled with a fantastic defensive typing, Bisharp's bulk allows it to tank attacks from some of the most common Pokemon in the tier, including Cyclizar, Noivern, and Jirachi, and use the turn to set up or strike back with its nigh-unresisted STAB combination. Sucker Punch elevates Bisharp into an incredibly threatening late-game cleaner after just one or two turns to set up, which Bisharp can easily gain through Terastallization. However, Bisharp suffers from a mediocre Speed stat that makes it slower than most other offensive threats and sweepers even with maximum Speed investment. The common Fighting-types in RU, including the likes of Terrakion and Mienshao, are therefore able to comfortably outspeed and KO Bisharp while taking little damage from Sucker Punch. Physical walls such as Gastrodon and Chesnaught can similarly tank Bisharp's attacks and strike back with super effective attacks. Lastly, Bisharp often finds itself wanting in terms of special bulk even with Eviolite, and it can often be taken out by strong special wallbreakers after minimal chip damage.
strategies.comments:
Other Options

Low Kick is a coverage option that can be used over Throat Chop to threaten opposing Bisharp, Registeel, and Crawdaunt more effectively. Tera Ghost gives Bisharp an immunity to Fighting, which can give it a free turn to set up against Fighting-type threats like Mienshao, Breloom, and Terrakion. The Ghost typing is particularly synergistic with Bisharp, as both of its weaknesses are naturally resisted by Bisharp, and it allows Bisharp to act as a spinblocker in a pinch for entry hazard stacking teams. However, Tera Ghost makes Bisharp weak to Knock Off, which can be very dangerous because it also neuters its bulk by removing Eviolite. Tera Grass combined with Tera Blast provides Bisharp with coverage for Quagsire and Gastrodon while also giving it a resistance to Earthquake. Tera Fairy is another option that provides valuable resistances to Fighting-, Dark-, and Bug-type attacks from the aforementioned Fighting-types.

Checks and Counters

Fighting-types: A myriad of Fighting-type wallbreakers, from common presences like Mienshao and Terrakion to niche picks like Lucario and Infernape, can comfortably tank even a +2 Sucker Punch and threaten Bisharp in turn with a KO. Chesnaught is a defensive Fighting-type that can reliably check Bisharp with its high physical bulk. However, all of these Pokemon should be wary of Terastallization, which can give Bisharp free turns to set up against them and potentially turn it into a game-ending threat.

Physical Walls: Certain physical walls, including Chesnaught, Quagsire, and Body Press Registeel, are able to tank Bisharp's attacks and threaten it with super effective attacks. Besides Chesnaught, they are usually unafraid of Terastallization due to their access to Unaware and Iron Defense, respectively, that can neutralize Bisharp's ability to set up.

Special Wallbreakers: Strong, bulky special attackers such as Magnezone and Choice Specs Hisuian Goodra are able to threaten Bisharp by targeting its middling special bulk. Magnet Pull Magnezone in particular can trap and eliminate Bisharp if it switches in safely.

Burn: Due to Bisharp's low Speed, it is prone to getting outsped and crippled by fast Will-O-Wisp users including Gengar. While Entei does not appreciate taking a +2 Sucker Punch, Sacred Fire from it can cripple even a Terastallized Bisharp.

movesets.name: Swords Dance
movesets.description:
Set Details

Swords Dance allows Bisharp to serve as a fantastic late-game sweeper. Sucker Punch provides strong priority that enables Bisharp to pick off weakened sweepers like Armarouge and improves its ability to clean. Eviolite drastically boosts Bisharp's ability to take hits, which can be invaluable for setting up. Defiant deters opposing Pokemon from using Defog and can potentially turn Bisharp into a deadly threat simply by getting Intimidated by Krookodile or switching into and receiving a stat drop from an attack like Gengar's Shadow Ball. 176 Speed EVs allow Bisharp to outspeed Modest Magnezone. Tera Flying flips Bisharp's matchup against Ground- and Fighting-type attacks, allowing it to stay in on Pokemon such as Krookodile, Terrakion, and Mienshao and use the turn to set up or grab a KO. Tera Dark is an option that instead boosts two of Bisharp's STAB attacks, which can be helpful for guaranteeing certain KOs such as unboosted Sucker Punch against Armarouge and +2 Throat Chop against Empoleon.

Swords Dance Bisharp is able to reliably fill the role of a bulky revenge killer and late-game sweeper on both balance and offense structures. Entry hazard stacking teams, with setters such as Krookodile, Jirachi, and Chesnaught, are able to gradually bring the opposing team into range of Bisharp's attacks by wearing them down, thus easing its job as a cleaner. At the same time, Bisharp fills the role of deterring Defog from users like Noivern. Offense, particularly hyper offense, teams can similarly take advantage of Defiant, as hazards like Stealth Rock and Sticky Web set by Pokemon such as Kleavor and Ribombee are likely to stick around. Other setup sweepers like Armarouge, Terrakion, and Mimikyu work well with Bisharp, as they can weaken or take out defensive Pokemon such as Hisuian Goodra, Slowbro, and Gastrodon and improve Bisharp's odds of sweeping. Bisharp is simultaneously able to serve as a revenge killer due to its access to Sucker Punch, which can be instrumental in hyper offense mirror matchups for taking care of threats like Armarouge and Gardevoir after they are weakened. A Ghost-type like Mimikyu or Weakness Policy Basculegion-F is also appreciated in these teams to block Rapid Spin from Cyclizar. Lastly, any of the fast Fighting-types in RU, such as Flamigo, Mienshao, and Terrakion, can easily tank a Sucker Punch and threaten Bisharp with an OHKO. Therefore, teammates that resist Fighting like Noivern, Slowbro, and Amoonguss can be invaluable partners for Bisharp in bulkier structures to prevent these wallbreakers from making too much progress.

strategies.overview:
Dark

Bisharp's Steel typing makes it an inviting piece for Dark teams looking to ease the Fairy matchup, as Bisharp can take on powerful Fairy-types such as Flutter Mane and Hatterene. In addition, its Defiant deters Defog from the likes of Corviknight and Galarian Weezing. However, Bisharp's middling Speed tier and mediocre bulk make it unable to switch into Fairy-type threats such as Enamorus and Mimikyu, and it needs a Swords Dance boost to reliably OHKO them. It is also helpless against Iron Valiant and other fast Fighting-types. The Defog users that Bisharp wishes to check like the aforementioned Corviknight and Galarian Weezing can similarly threaten Bisharp on a predicted switch with Body Press and Will-O-Wisp, respectively.

movesets.name: Eviolite Swords Dance (Steel)
movesets.description:
When paired with an Eviolite, Bisharp is capable of taking on the role of a bulky setup sweeper that also discourages the use of Defog. Additonally, Bisharp's Dark typing allows Eviolite to ease the matchup against Ghost teams by letting Bisharp take on their Ghost-type STAB moves better with its improved bulk. Throat Chop serves as its primary Dark-type STAB move and deals great damage to bulkier threats like Sinistcha and Gholdengo. Sucker Punch boosted by Swords Dance allows Bisharp to KO faster Pokemon like Dragapult, Hoopa-U, and Choice item Spectrier, while Low Kick allows it to threaten opposing Bisharp as well as doing good damage to Ting-Lu and defensive Heatran. Iron Head can also be ran as an option over Low Kick to shut down certain Fairy-types like Primarina and Clefable, which would otherwise check Bisharp. 80 HP and 20 Defense EVs paired with Eviolite allow Bisharp to avoid getting 2HKOed by Ogerpon-W's Ivy Cudgel and survive a Belly Drum-boosted Azumarill's Aqua Jet and an Earthquake from most common Garchomp sets. 176 Speed EV allows Bisharp to outspeed Modest Magnezone.

Skarmory is one of Bisharp's greatest allies, as it can defensively switch into Ground- and Fighting-types like Excadrill, Great Tusk, and Urshifu-R easily. Skarmory also sets Spikes, which chips down walls like Hippowdon and Archaludon into Bisharp's KO range and makes picking off frailer Pokemon with Sucker Punch easier. Gholdengo can check scary Fairy-types like Iron Valiant while also absorbing hits from threats like Sneasler and Hisuian Lilligant without risk thanks to Good as Gold blocking a potential Switcheroo or Sleep Powder, respectively. In return, Bisharp can remove opposing Ghost-types like opposing Gholdengo and Choice Scarf Hisuian Zoroark. Heatran is a great partner for Bisharp, as its Fire immunity allows it to take on threats like Volcarona, Iron Moth, and Ninetales while also being able to wear down or KO physical walls like Skarmory, Amoonguss, and Toxapex. Archaludon's utility allows Bisharp to break through its foes more easily with Stealth Rock while also letting it outspeed crucial Pokemon like the Ogerpon formes and Enamorus with Thunder Wave. Archaludon can also use Choice Scarf to help remove checks to Bisharp like Iron Valiant and wear down faster threats like Ogerpon-H so that they are in Bisharp's KO range. Iron Treads's access to Rapid Spin allows Bisharp to not get worn down by entry hazards, and it also checks potential threats to Bisharp like opposing Heatran and Landorus with Earthquake and Ice Spinner.

movesets.name: Eviolite Swords Dance (Dark)
movesets.description:
Bisharp's extra bulk provided by Eviolite allows it to lure in unsuspecting checks to the non-Eviolite Bisharp set such as Ogerpon-H and Choice Specs Flutter Mane and set up on them with Swords Dance or KO them outright. Furthermore, its Steel typing is incredibly valuable, as it enables it to take Fairy-type attacks for its teammates while also hitting Fairy-types very hard with its own Steel-type STAB move. Defiant allows Bisharp to fulfill its role as a Defog dissuader and also punish the use of Sticky Web from the likes of Galvantula and Araquanid. Throat Chop, when paired with Swords Dance, deals great damage to bulkier threats like Raging Bolt. Sucker Punch lets Bisharp KO fast Pokemon like Dragapult, Hoopa-U, and Choice item Spectrier, while Iron Head removes Fairy-types like Primarina and Hatterene. 80 HP and 20 Defense EVs allow Bisharp to avoid a 2HKO from Ogerpon-W's Ivy Cudgel and survive an Earthquake from non-Choice Band Mamoswine. 176 Speed EVs allow Bisharp to outspeed maximum Speed Modest Magnezone while also surviving Azumarill's boosted Aqua Jet thanks to the bulk granted by Eviolite.

Bisharp appreciates Spikes setters like Ting-Lu and Hisuian Samurott, as the chip damage allows it to break through bulkier targets like Archaludon and Hippowdon more easily. Both Spikes setters also help Bisharp break through the aforementioned walls by wearing them down with Ruination and Sacred Sword. Strong special attackers like Greninja and Darkrai help Bisharp by breaking down physical walls like Skarmory and defensive Great Tusk while also using their high Speed and Psychic-type coverage to remove Fighting-types like Iron Valiant and Keldeo. Sableye acts as a good defensive switch-in to Fighting-type attacks and spreads burns to physical Fighting-type attackers like Sneasler and Iron Hands. Additionally, Sableye crucially can burn Skarmory, which prevents Bisharp from being OHKOed by its Body Press. Sableye also utilizes Encore to disrupt opposing setup attempts, granting Bisharp the ability to safely switch in. Meowscarada can use its Protean-boosted Triple Axel or Play Rough to check speedy threats like Roaring Moon while also breaking through bulkier Pokemon like Great Tusk and Swampert. Mandibuzz acts as a great support for Bisharp, as it can take Fighting- and Ground-type attacks easily thanks to its part-Flying typing, use Defog to remove entry hazards, and pivot with U-turn to get Bisharp safely onto the field. Alolan Muk acts as a good special sponge that can take hits from Enamorus and Kyurem while using Knock Off to remove items like Choice Specs, allowing Bisharp to handle them better with its Eviolite-boosted bulk.

movesets.name: Swords Dance (Dark)
movesets.description:
Bisharp serves a niche role on Dark teams with its secondary Steel typing and Defiant ability enabling it to take on the bulky Calm Mind Fairy-types of the tier such as Primarina and Clefable and punish Defog from the likes of Mandibuzz or Sticky Web from Araquanid or Galvantula, respectively. At +2 Attack, Iron Head can OHKO Fairy-types such as Hatterene, Galarian Weezing, and Clefable. Throat Chop enables Bisharp to dish out immense damage to the likes of Skarmory and Toxapex. Lastly, Sucker Punch helps mitigate Bisharp's low Speed, allowing it to check threats such as Flutter Mane and Iron Moth. Life Orb gives Bisharp a much desired power boost; however, Black Glasses can be used to allow Bisharp to stick around for a bit longer while still OHKOing Flutter Mane with Sucker Punch after entry hazard chip damage.

Greninja and Darkrai support Bisharp by being able to remove physical walls such as Skarmory, Archaludon, and defensive Great Tusk along with using their Psychic-type coverage to threaten Fighting-types such as Keldeo and Iron Valiant. Sableye provides a crucial Fighting immunity, enabling it to handle threats such as Gallade, Sneasler, and Iron Hands along with being able to burn Skarmory, preventing Bisharp from getting OHKOed by Body Press. Ting-Lu provides entry hazards to wear down physically bulky targets such as Archaludon and Hippowdon. Alolan Muk is also not weak to Fairy and can reliably take on foes such as Enamorus and Primarina along with handling other special attackers like Kyurem. Choice Scarf Meowscarada provides an incredible Speed tier and supports Bisharp by taking out threats such as Quaquaval and Great Tusk while using Protean Play Rough or Triple Axel to handle Dragon-types such as Roaring Moon and Raging Bolt. Mandibuzz is immune to Ground and can safely bring Bisharp in with U-turn and clear hazards with Defog.

movesets.name: Swords Dance (Steel)
movesets.description:
Bisharp serves as an incredible offensive threat on Steel teams thanks to its Dark typing and strong priority in Sucker Punch, which can enable Bisharp to handle threats such as Dragapult and Hoopa-U. Throat Chop pressures Ghost- and Psychic-types such as Gholdengo, Sinistcha, and Galarian Slowking. Low Kick allows Bisharp to deal with opposing Bisharp along with dealing solid damage to Ting-Lu. Alternatively, Iron Head can be used to deal with Fairy-types like Primarina and Galarian Weezing. Life Orb is used to provide Bisharp a crucial boost, enabling it to OHKO Flutter Mane with Sucker Punch, but Black Glasses can be used to enable Bisharp to stick around longer over the course of a game while still maintaining its ability to 2HKO threats like Toxapex with a +2 Throat Chop.

Bisharp greatly appreciates support from Skarmory, which can come in on Ground- and Fighting-types such as Excadrill, Great Tusk, and Iron Hands and can easily take them on with a combination of Iron Defense and Body Press. Skarmory can also set Spikes, enhancing Bisharp's breaking capabilities by allowing it to power through threats such as Archaludon and Hippowdon. Gholdengo can easily take on Fighting-types like Sneasler, Iron Hands, and Breloom thanks to its Ghost typing along with being able to remove Fairy-types like Iron Valiant and Galarian Weezing. In return, Bisharp can remove opposing Ghost-types such as Flutter Mane and opposing Gholdengo. Heatran's Fire immunity lets it handle Fire-types such as Iron Moth, Ninetales, and Volcarona, and it is able to remove physically bulky walls such as Archaludon and Skarmory. Archaludon provides Stealth Rock support along with being able to use Thunder Wave, enabling for Bisharp to outspeed targets such as the Ogerpon formes. Iron Treads provides entry hazard removal to give Bisharp safe entry while being able to remove threats such as Raging Bolt, Heatran, and Okidogi. Hisuian Goodra provides a solid special wall that can take on threats such as Hydreigon and Primarina that can handle Bisharp.

movesets.name: Swords Dance
movesets.description: Swords Dance Bisharp is a fearsome wallbreaker and sweeper, utilizing its powerful STAB combination and decent defensive profile to threaten notable defensive staples such as Clefable, Aegislash, and Amoonguss. Besides serving as Bisharp's strongest STAB option to use against neutral targets such as Rotom-W, Celesteela, and Skarmory, Knock Off also comes with the benefit of removing held items from common switch-ins such as Buzzwole and Keldeo, which allows Bisharp to more easily break past them later. Sucker Punch is a powerful priority move that lets Bisharp threaten more offensive teams, notably KOing common attackers such as Iron Boulder and Mega Gardevoir after minimal chip damage or Swords Dance, respectively. Iron Head is Bisharp's strongest STAB option against Mega Venusaur, common Z-Move users such as Hydrapple, and Fairy-types like Clefable. An Adamant nature maximizes Bisharp's power, securing 2HKOs on physically defensive Pokemon such as Tangrowth and Hippowdon after Swords Dance. Alternatively, a Jolly nature lets Bisharp get the jump on faster Rotom-W variants as well as Aegislash with a Speed-boosting nature. Life Orb is Bisharp's item of choice for powering up all of its moves, ensuring that +2 Knock Off can OHKO the bulkiest Rotom-W while giving +2 Iron Head good odds to OHKO offensive Mega Venusaur after Stealth Rock. Alternatively, Black Glasses forfeits the added power on Iron Head in favor of avoiding recoil damage; it should be noted that the power boost it provides on Bisharp's Dark-type attacks can still be crucial, notably allowing it to secure the OHKO on Mega Gallade, Mega Aerodactyl, and utility Excadrill with +2 Sucker Punch. Finally, Eviolite can be used if the added power of the aforementioned options isn't a concern. The added defensive security lets Bisharp survive attacks such as Enamorus's Earth Power and Choice Scarf Hydreigon's Fire Blast from full HP. Additionally, if Bisharp runs the alternative EV spread, it can also take on Excadrill's Earthquake after Stealth Rock and Iron Moth's Fiery Dance while still outpacing Adamant Tyranitar. With its combination of offensive traits, powerful priority, and typing, Bisharp fits on a variety of offense and hyper offense teams. Entry hazard setters such as Mold Breaker Excadrill, Swampert, and Mew make for excellent pairings, as their ability to accrue chip damage on physically bulky Pokemon such as Skarmory and Tangrowth can help a boosted Bisharp break through them more easily; in return, Bisharp can use Defiant ability to capitalize on Defog from utility Serperior and Rotom-W, forcing them into uncomfortable situations. By extension, Ribombee is also a notable partner, as its Sticky Web support can let Bisharp outpace targets such as Life Orb Mienshao and Booster Energy Iron Moth, preventing them from being effective offensive checks. Other setup sweepers such as Autotomize Celesteela, Dragon Dance Mega Aerodactyl, and Swords Dance users such as Aegislash and Scizor work well with Bisharp: in tandem, they can assist each other in overwhelming shared defensive checks such as Buzzwole and Hippowdon. Against more offensive teams, Aegislash and Scizor can also use their own priority attacks to weaken faster Pokemon like Keldeo, Hydreigon, and Okidogi to the pointwhere Bisharp can pick them off with Sucker Punch more easily.

movesets.name: Pursuit Trapper
movesets.description: With its good defensive typing and powerful Dark-type attacks, Bisharp is a prime user of Pursuit, able to trap offensive threats like Aegislash and Choice Band Iron Boulder as well as weakened defensive Pokemon like Slowking and Skeledirge. Notably, Bisharp also gains an Attack boost from Aegislash's King's Shield, courtesy of Defiant, making Bisharp much more reliable at trapping Aegislash as a result. Knock Off is Bisharp's strongest STAB option, and it removes held items, permanently crippling Dark-type checks such as Keldeo and Buzzwole. Sucker Punch is a strong priority move that lets Bisharp threaten chipped offensive Pokemon such as Iron Moth, Thundurus, and Zeraora, and it can also OHKO Swords Dance Iron Boulder from full. Additionally, even though Psychic-type Pokemon like Mega Latias and Alakazam have the means to naturally outspeed and threaten Bisharp with Fighting-type coverage, the threat of being KOed by Sucker Punch in doing so means Bisharp can potentially Pursuit trap them as well. Iron Head provides Bisharp with a strong secondary STAB move that hits Fairy-type Pokemon like Clefable and Azumarill as well as other Pokemon that don't mind taking a Knock Off, like Mega Venusaur, for decent damage. Choice Band further inflates Bisharp's huge Attack stat, making it more difficult to check with Pokemon such as Amoonguss and Hippowdon while giving Bisharp an easier time eliminating bulkier targets like Aegislash and Slowbro with Pursuit. Maximum Attack and Speed investment in conjunction with an Adamant nature is used with Choice Band to make Bisharp as fast and strong as possible. However, a Jolly nature trades a portion of said attacking power in favor of outspeeding faster Rotom-W variants as well as Aegislash and Magnezone with Speed-boosting natures. On sets with Eviolite, an alternative EV spread of 52 HP / 244 Atk / 28 SpD / 184 Spe should be used to let Bisharp survive Excadrill's Earthquake after Stealth Rock and Iron Moth's Fiery Dance while still outpacing Adamant Tyranitar. Pursuit Bisharp is best used on bulky offense and balance teams as an offensive threat that also provides valuable utility against Aegislash as well as Psychic-types like Choice Band Iron Boulder, Slowbro, and Slowking, preventing them from making excessive progress throughout the match. Wallbreakers such as Mega Gardevoir, Keldeo, and Iron Moth benefit the most from this support, as Aegislash and several of the aforementioned Psychic-types are often used to answer them in some form. Bisharp removing these threats allows these wallbreakers to become far more offensively threatening, and in return, they can help Bisharp pressure physically defensive checks such as Buzzwole and Skarmory. While Bisharp possesses a strong Sucker Punch to threaten more offensive foes, it can also be quite unreliable, being resisted by common offensive threats such as Mienshao, Enamorus, and Keldeo, and it's easily taken advantage of by setup sweepers like Autotomize Celesteela and Booster Energy Iron Moth. For this reason, Bisharp pairs fantastically with speed control options such as Mega Aerodactyl, Zeraora, and Choice Scarf users like Enamorus that can help check these Pokemon. Lastly, defensive pivots such as Scizor, Rotom-W, and Slowbro are integral to Bisharp's success, allowing it to enter the field safely against its desired targets. Safe entry is especially important when factoring in how some of Bisharp's targets like Aegislash and Slowbro have the means to outright KO or cripple it with Close Combat and Scald burns, respectively, before it can be Pursuit trap them.
